questions.stem: The values of \(x\) for which the angle between the vectors \(\vec{a} = 2x^2\hat{i} + 4x\hat{j} + \hat{k}\) and \(\vec{b} = 7\hat{i} - 2\hat{j} + x\hat{k}\) is obtuse, is :
If a line makes angles of \(\dfrac{3\pi}{4}, \dfrac{\pi}{3}\) and \(\theta\) with the positive directions of \(x\), y and z-axis respectively, then \(\theta\) is
questions._flag: DEFECTIVE QUESTION, and CBSE says so itself. The official marking scheme for THIS set (ms/p02, printed page 3 of 25) prints for Q2, in place of an answer: "No option is correct. Full marks may be awarded for attempting the question." My independent derivation agrees: cos^2(3pi/4) + cos^2(pi/3) + cos^2(theta) = 1/2 + 1/4 + cos^2(theta) = 1 gives cos(theta) = +/- 1/2, so theta = pi/3 or 2pi/3. A direction angle lies in [0, pi], which rules out the negative branch in (A) and (D); (B) is incomplete because it drops 2pi/3; (C) is simply wrong. This is the SAME defective block that 65/2/1 printed as its Q6, and CBSE declared it keyless on both sets. Transcribed as printed with no answer and _noCorrectOption set.
